hook_text: A litre of fresh milk and a bag of milk powder are the same food. Only one of them can go to a refugee camp.
clip_script: Lay out the food and ask five questions. Does it keep without a fridge? Is it nourishing? Does it travel light? Can you cook it in a big pot with little fuel? Will these people eat it? Fresh milk: sours in a day, fails. Milk powder: a year in the bag, a tenth of the weight, passes. Bread: two days. Maize meal: months in a sack, pap in twenty minutes, passes everything, first on every food parcel. Processing is the trick. Dry it and the mould has no water. Mill it and it cooks fast. Tin it and it keeps for years, though it weighs. Fortify it and every bowl of pap carries vitamin A and iron. The list writes itself: maize meal, rice, beans, pilchards, oil, tinned tomatoes, onions, cabbage. Then soften it for babies and grandmothers, swap pork for fish where needed, and count the firewood.
visual_style: Whiteboard table of foods with five tick columns; milk and milk powder side by side; a tin, a sack and a bag with keep-times; a four-group list filling in.
mood: Curious and practical, judging food like an engineer.
pacing: Questions, milk, powder, bread, meal, processes, list, adjust, each a beat.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and ask the five questions of what is in your kitchen.
